title: ISMS and ISO 27001: which certificate do you need, and will the system run your security?
short: Certify only what customers or regulators ask for, scope all relevant operations and review risks with management at least once a year.
answer: Decide this quarter which evidence your customers and regulators actually ask for, such as an ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate or a TISAX label, because NIS2 and the German BSIG require documented measures, not a certificate[^bsiiso]. Then scope the ISMS to all the regulated entity's relevant operations, let your risk register choose the controls and have management decide on the remaining risks at least once a year.
audience: Security, compliance and IT leads in EU organizations, especially in Germany, deciding whether and how to build an ISMS

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: List who asks for which evidence.
items.text: Write down what key customers, regulators and insurers require. The BSI calls an ISO 27001 certificate a good foundation for the BSIG but no proof of NIS2 compliance[^bsiiso].

items.title: Scope the whole regulated entity.
items.text: ISO 27001 lets you limit the scope; the BSIG requires measures for all relevant operations of the entity[^bsiiso]. Include IT operations, cloud services and outsourced process steps.

items.title: Let risks choose the controls.
items.text: Derive controls from risk treatment, then check them against Annex A so none is left out by accident[^iaf26]. Under the BSIG, you can't just accept or transfer a relevant risk[^bsiiso].

items.title: Make management own the remaining risks.
items.text: ISMS responsibility can't be delegated, and management signs off residual risks[^std3001]. Give every accepted risk an owner and an end date.

items.title: Audit whether controls work.
items.text: Give internal auditors time to test the controls for your biggest risks[^std3001]: restore a backup, sample leavers' accounts, trigger an alert.

items.title: Does a regulator name a scheme?
items.text: German power and gas grid operators need an ISMS certified against the Bundesnetzagentur's 2015 IT security catalog, now under revision; an ISO or IT-Grundschutz certificate alone isn't enough[^bnetza]. Other KRITIS operators prove their measures to the BSI every 3 years[^bsig].

items.title: Do automotive customers ask for TISAX?
items.text: More than ten vehicle makers and thousands of suppliers use TISAX results to judge partners[^enxisa]. Register the sites and objectives your customer names.

items.title: Do customers or tenders ask for ISO 27001?
items.text: Get an accredited ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate, which can be recognized worldwide[^iaf26].

items.title: Do you want the BSI's catalog behind it?
items.text: ISO 27001 on the basis of IT-Grundschutz needs a BSI-certified lead auditor; the BSI checks the report and issues the certificate[^bsischema].

items.title: Does nobody ask for a certificate?
items.text: Build to ISO 27001 anyway and certify when asked. NIST CSF 2.0 helps report outcomes to the board, but NIST offers no certification[^nistfaq].

blocks.title: The certifiable options side by side
blocks.intro: ENISA maps each requirement of NIS2 Implementing Regulation 2024/2690 to ISO 27001 and NIST CSF 2.0, without judging equivalence or full coverage[^enisatig].

columns.title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022
items: **Current edition.** The 2022 text with Amendment 1:2024[^iso27001], which asks you to decide whether climate change is relevant; no new certificate is needed[^iafclimate].
**Controls.** Annex A refers to the 93 controls of ISO/IEC 27002:2022[^iaf26]. You select them by risk and list them in the statement of applicability (SoA).
**2013 is gone.** Certificates to the 2013 edition expired or were withdrawn by 31 October 2025[^iaf26].

columns.title: IT-Grundschutz and Grundschutz++
items: **Classic.** Audited against BSI-Standard 200-2 and the Kompendium Edition 2023[^bsipruef], for 3 years with yearly surveillance[^bsischema]. Certifiable until 30 November 2031[^gspp].
**Grundschutz++.** BSI-Standard 300-1 sets the method and a machine-readable catalog replaces the Kompendium. Certification applications open on 1 January 2027[^gspp].
**Less risk work.** For normal protection needs the BSI did the risk analysis; you cover high needs and gaps[^std3001].

columns.title: TISAX
items: **Objectives set the depth.** AL2 checks evidence and interviews the security lead, usually by video call. AL3, for example for strictly confidential data and prototype parts, checks everything, generally on site[^tisaxnis2].
**Catalog.** VDA ISA2027 applies to assessments ordered from 1 January 2027[^enxisa]; initial ISA6 assessments can be opened until March 2027[^enxdl].
**Validity.** Labels last up to 3 years[^enxisa].

blocks.title: What NIS2 and the BSIG require
items: **No certificate.** The BSI says ISO 27001 certification is no precondition for meeting the BSIG[^bsiiso], and IT-Grundschutz isn't mandatory for all entities[^bsifaq].

**Documented measures.** You must document how you meet the risk management duties[^bsig] and show proof when the BSI orders it, for example audit reports. KRITIS operators submit it unasked[^bsifaq].

**Gaps to close.** Registration, reporting deadlines and management training aren't part of ISO 27001[^bsiiso]; see the EU security laws sheet. Energy and telecom operators follow their sector law instead[^bsig].

**Mappings are gap lists.** The BSI maps each § 30 BSIG measure to ISO 27001 clauses and controls[^bsiiso]. ENX, which runs TISAX, argues that a label covering all affected sites meets NIS2 apart from reporting[^tisaxnis2]; the BSI says no company certificate alone meets every BSIG requirement[^bsifaq].

blocks.title: Scope and SoA, done honestly
items: **Scope by business process.** Name the processes, sites, applications, IT systems and service providers, and include each process completely[^std3001].

**Mark each control's real state.** Implemented with evidence, planned with a date, or not applicable. Grundschutz++ allows that only if a requirement can't functionally be met or the component is absent, with a reason[^std3001].
**Explain every choice.** ISA2027 requires each listed aspect to be consciously considered and the decision explainable[^enxisa]. Hold your SoA to that.

**Keep the documents few.** Scope, policy, objectives, risk register, SoA, treatment plan, audit and corrective action records and review minutes. Management approves the policy; every employee gets it[^std3001].

blocks.title: Run a risk assessment that changes decisions
items: **Management sets the limits.** It approves the method, acceptance criteria and risk appetite[^std3001]. Write criteria in euros, days of downtime and records exposed.

**Start with the crown jewels.** Rate each business process for confidentiality, integrity and availability; Grundschutz++ advises starting with the most important one in the highest category[^std3001].
**Process owners own risks.** That is the default unless you decide otherwise[^std3001]. Link each risk to measures with an owner and a due date.
**Sign off and repeat.** Risk owners approve the plan and management the residual risks. Review at least yearly and after significant changes[^std3001] or serious incidents.

blocks.title: Audits and reviews that change things
items: **Aim audits at your risks.** Plan the program around the top risks, detection and incident handling, and earlier findings[^std3001]. Test real samples.
**Look for improvements.** Grundschutz++ sees internal audit as a way to find improvements, not just nonconformities[^std3001].
**Keep it impartial.** Pick an objective audit team and keep the security officer role apart from IT management[^std3001].
**End the review with decisions.** Cover audit results, performance, incidents, risk treatment, threat changes and earlier decisions[^std3001]. Record decisions on budget, scope and accepted risks.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Grundschutz++ arrived.** BSI-Standard 300-1 version 1.0, dated 20 October 2026, targets experienced early adopters[^std3001]. Certification applications on its basis open on 1 January 2027; classic IT-Grundschutz certification ends on 30 November 2031[^gspp].

**TISAX moved to yearly catalogs.** Under ISA2027, published on 1 July 2026, suppliers to organizations with very high protection needs are expected to show a TISAX label, an equivalent assessment or a supplier audit. New catalogs follow each summer[^enxisa].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **A policy for every Annex A control.** Write rules where people need them; for technical controls, configuration exports are better evidence.
**A GRC tool before the first cycle.** A spreadsheet register and your ticket system will do.
**Separate programs for ISO, TISAX and NIS2.** Keep one register and one SoA with a column for each mapping.
**Waiting for Grundschutz++.** Its method requirements mirror ISO 27001 clauses 4 to 10[^std3001], so scope, risk and audit work carries over.
**A climate change study.** Record whether it is relevant and why; IAF treats the amendment as a clarification[^iafclimate].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **A scope too narrow to matter.** A certificate for the IT department alone misses what customers and the BSI care about. The BSI tells certified entities to check whether NIS2 needs a wider scope[^bsiiso].
**Controls copied from a template.** An SoA with every control implemented and no evidence falls apart in the first customer audit.

**An ISMS run only by consultants.** Management can't hand over responsibility, and a security role must be involved in security-relevant projects such as new systems[^std3001]. Let consultants coach the process owners.
**Trusting a supplier's logo.** Ask for the certificate's scope and SoA; see the third-party risk sheet.

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Build to ISO 27001 without certifying until a customer asks.
Name a security officer with budgeted time and a deputy.
Hold the risk review and management review in one half-day meeting a year.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Certify where customers ask, then widen the scope to the whole regulated entity.
Check your SoA against the BSI's § 30 BSIG mapping[^bsiiso] and, for digital providers, ENISA's table[^enisatig].
Test one top-risk control each quarter.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Align certification audits with the 3-yearly KRITIS proof to the BSI[^bsig].
With many sites and a central ISMS, ask about a TISAX simplified group assessment[^tisaxnis2].
Report effectiveness measures to the board quarterly.

changes.text: Published after a copy edit and a source-by-source fact check, which narrowed 13 statements to what the sources say.
First draft, based on BSI-Standard 300-1, the BSIG and BSI NIS-2 guidance, IAF MD 26, ENX's ISA2027 and NIS2 analysis, ENISA's mapping and NIST CSF 2.0.
